q: What makes Tanzania one of the best safari destinations?
a: Tanzania offers world-class parks such as Serengeti, Ngorongoro Crater, Tarangire, and Lake Manyara, giving visitors unmatched wildlife diversity.

q: Which national parks are most popular?
a: The most visited include Serengeti, Ngorongoro Crater, Tarangire, Selous/Nyerere, and Lake Manyara.

q: How many days do I need for a good safari?
a: A minimum of 4–6 days is ideal, but 7–10 days offers the best experience with multiple parks.

q: Can I choose between private and group safaris?
a: Yes. You can book a fully private safari or join a small group depending on availability and preference.

q: What is a typical safari day like?
a: Days usually include early morning game drives, lunch in the bush or lodge, and afternoon or sunset game drives.

q: Are safaris good for first-time travelers?
a: Yes. Tanzania safaris are safe, well-organized, and perfect for first-time visitors to Africa.

q: How experienced are your guides?
a: Professional guides have years of experience in wildlife tracking, driving, and park knowledge.

q: Why is the Serengeti so famous?
a: It hosts the Great Wildebeest Migration, one of the world’s greatest wildlife spectacles.

q: Can I customize my safari itinerary?
a: Absolutely — tours can be tailored based on your interests, days, and budget.

q: What is the difference between a game drive and safari?
a: A safari is the overall trip; a game drive is the activity of searching for wildlife inside the park.

q: When is the best time for safari?
a: The dry season (June–October) offers the best wildlife visibility.

q: When is the Great Migration?
a: It moves year-round, with river crossings July–October.

q: When is the calving season?
a: January–March in the Ndutu area.

q: When is the low season?
a: March–May — good for budget travelers.

q: When is the best time to visit Zanzibar?
a: June–October and December–February.

q: How do I book a safari?
a: You can book by contacting us via email, WhatsApp, or our website booking form.

q: When is final payment due?
a: Final payment is made upon arrival in Tanzania, and you can pay by cash, card, or bank transfer, depending on what is most convenient for you. We will provide full payment instructions during your booking confirmation to ensure a smooth process.

q: What payment methods are accepted?
a: Bank transfer, credit cards, online payment gateways, and mobile money

q: Are there hidden costs?
a: No. All costs are clearly listed; optional extras are explained before booking.

q: Can I book last minute?
a: Yes, depending on accommodation availability.

q: What clothing should I pack?
a: Neutral-colored clothes, comfortable shirts, shorts, long sleeves, and a warm jacket.

q: Are bright colors okay?
a: Avoid bright colors; they can attract insects or disturb wildlife.

q: Do I need warm clothes?
a: Yes — mornings and evenings can be cold.

q: What personal items should I bring?
a: Sunscreen, insect repellent, sunglasses, and personal medications.

q: How much luggage is allowed on small planes?
a: Usually 15–20 kg per person.

q: What types of lodges are available?
a: Budget, mid-range, luxury lodges, and tented camps.

q: Are tented camps safe?
a: Yes. Camps follow strict safety measures and have 24/7 security.

q: Do rooms have private bathrooms?
a: Most mid-range and luxury camps offer en-suite bathrooms.

q: Are meals included?
a: Yes — breakfast, lunch, and dinner are included.

q: Do rooms have private bathrooms?
a: Most mid-range and luxury camps offer en-suite bathrooms.
